summary: Users experience 401 invalid_token on ~36% of /token/validate calls, beginning sharply in the 14:00 bucket (auth-service error rate 0.22% -> 30.52%, sustained ~36%; api-gateway logs 466 'auth-service ... 401 invalid_token'). Two changes landed within one minute: dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0, JWT lib 0.11->0.12 'breaking parser API' + TokenValidator rewritten) at 14:00:00Z, and cfg-2705 (signing-key rotation k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04) at 14:01:00Z. The deploy precedes the config change and the onset, favoring the bad deployment (H1); the config rotation (H2) is one minute too late. Infra/resource causes are ruled out (redis-cache, user-db, auth CPU/mem/restarts all flat). Best hypothesis: bad_deployment dep-5710 with a rewritten JWT validator selectively rejecting valid tokens (mirrors HIST-109). Confidence 0.62 because auth-service logs are unavailable (pipeline down), so I cannot see the exact validation failure to fully separate it from the key-rotation cause.

ranked_hypotheses.title: JWT library upgrade / TokenValidator rewrite (dep-5710) rejects a subset of valid tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service v7.3.0 deployed at 14:00 refactored token validation and upgraded jjwt 0.11->0.12 with a 'breaking parser API'. The rewritten validator mis-validates a subset of otherwise-valid tokens (e.g. changed clock-skew/claim-parsing behavior), producing persistent 401 invalid_token for ~36% of /token/validate calls. Fault originates in the auth-service release.

causal_chain.claim: auth-service error rate jumps in the same 14:00 bucket (0.22%->30.52%)
downstream symptom surfaces as 401 invalid_token on /token/validate at the gateway
partial, stable ~36% failure with no resource/infra anomaly is consistent with selective validation logic failure

assumptions: A code path in the rewritten validator selectively fails tokens (e.g. skew/claim handling), which could not be confirmed because auth-service logs are unavailable.
The error_rate metric labeled '5xx' actually reflects the observed 401 failures.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Scheduled signing-key rotation (cfg-2705) invalidated a subset of tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-2705 rotated jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04, publishing a new key id before all pods/validators loaded it (as in HIST-108), causing a fraction of tokens to be validated against the wrong key and return 401 invalid_token.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 rotated the signing key id at 14:01:00Z
tokens validated against a not-yet-propagated key return 401 invalid_token

assumptions: Key distribution is per-pod and lagged, so only some validations fail.
The rotation, though timestamped 14:01, could have been applied/effective slightly before its recorded time.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared dependency (redis-cache) or infrastructure degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared datastore (redis-cache) or infrastructure fault degraded auth-service token validation, causing 401s.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: redis-cache hit_ratio/memory/evictions and user-db CPU were all flat through onset; no infra anomaly (F6, F7, F5).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource exhaustion / capacity saturation on auth-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service ran out of CPU/memory/connections or was overloaded, producing validation failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU ~38%, memory ~52%, request_rate ~400 req/s, restarts 0 all unchanged at onset (F5); failures are deterministic 401s not timeouts.

assumptions: The 14:00 error-rate jump and the gateway 401s are the same event.
cfg-2705's recorded timestamp approximates when it took effect (it postdates onset, weakening it as the cause).
Neither dep-5710 nor cfg-2705 was rolled back before the current time (both show rolled_back_at: null).

timeline.event: dep-5710 auth-service v7.3.0 deployed (jjwt 0.11->0.12 breaking parser API; TokenValidator rewritten)
auth-service error_rate jumps 0.22% -> 30.52%, api-gateway error_rate 0.16% -> 17.67% in the same bucket
cfg-2705 signing-key rotation k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 (one minute after onset)
INC-007 reported; ~36% error rate sustained through 15:48

recommended_actions.action: Roll back auth-service to the pre-dep-5710 version (v7.3.0 -> previous) and confirm 401 rate drops within one bucket.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy is the earliest change and the leading hypothesis; a rollback is the fastest way to confirm cause and restore service. If 401s persist after rollback, escalate to H2 (key rotation).

recommended_actions.action: If rollback is not possible, prepare a compatibility fix for the jjwt 0.12 parser rewrite, especially clock-skew and claim-parsing defaults; pin explicit skew config.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-109 was the same class of regression fixed by pinning skew config.

recommended_actions.action: In parallel, verify JWKS/key propagation: check that all auth-service pods loaded k-2026-04 and consider re-publishing the previous key id if rotation is implicated.
recommended_actions.rationale: H2 is the live alternative; key-id mismatch produces identical 401 invalid_token symptoms (HIST-108).

recommended_actions.action: Restore the identity namespace log pipeline so auth-service validation errors become searchable; without it root cause cannot be fully confirmed.
recommended_actions.rationale: auth-service logs returned 503, blocking direct confirmation of the exact validation failure.

data_gaps: auth-service logs are unretrievable (backend 503, identity log pipeline down) - cannot see the exact validator error (key-not-found vs skew/claim vs parse failure) that would definitively separate H1 from H2.
error_rate metric is labeled '% of requests (HTTP 5xx)' yet the observed failures are 401s; the metric's semantics vs true 401 count are unconfirmed.
No per-key or per-pod breakdown of which tokens fail, so the '~1/3 partial' scope cannot be attributed to a specific key, pod, or token cohort.
No access to auth-service internal logs to confirm whether dep-5710 introduced a skew/claim regression versus a JWKS/propagation issue.

findings.statement: auth-service error rate jumped sharply from ~0.22% to 30.52% in the 14:00 bucket and stayed near 36% through 15:48 (last 38.23%).
api-gateway logs show 466 WARN entries, all the same pattern 'auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token', first seen 14:02:22Z.
A deployment of auth-service (dep-5710, v7.3.0) landed at 14:00:00Z whose changes are 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)' and 'TokenValidator rewritten'; it is still live and not rolled back.
A config change cfg-2705 rotated auth-service jwt.signing.key_id from k-2025-10 to k-2026-04 at 14:01:00Z, one minute AFTER incident onset.
auth-service resource metrics were flat across onset: CPU ~38% (37.9-38.7), memory ~52% (51.25-52.89), restarts 0, request_rate ~400 req/s unchanged, latency_p99 ~90ms unchanged.
Shared datastore redis-cache was healthy and unchanged across onset: hit_ratio ~96%, memory ~70%, evictions ~3/min.
user-db CPU stayed flat ~18% across onset, ruling out a database-side fault.
auth-service logs are NOT retrievable: query returned backend_unavailable 503 after 3 attempts (matching the report's note that the identity log pipeline is down).
api-gateway error rate also jumped at 14:00 (0.16% -> 17.67%, sustained ~21%), while its latency_p99 stayed flat ~210ms.
No JWKS/key/expired-related log lines were found in api-gateway logs (searches for 'jwks', 'key', 'expired' all returned 0 matches).
Historical incident HIST-109 (2025-07-11) matches this symptom set: '401 invalid_token' after a JWT library upgrade that changed clock-skew default, category bad_deployment.

refs.quote: JWT library upgrade changed clock-skew default

findings.statement: Historical incident HIST-108 (2025-10-01) matches the alternative: '401s after JWT signing key rotation', category config_change, caused by publishing a new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS.

refs.quote: Key rotation published new key id before all pods loaded the JWKS
